headline: Fire Hits LTO-NCR Office in Quezon City; Cause and Damage Still Undetermined
seoTitle: Fire Hits LTO-NCR Office on G. Araneta Avenue, Quezon City | FMB News
seoDescription: A first-alarm fire broke out Sunday morning at the LTO-NCR office on G. Araneta Avenue in Quezon City. The fire’s origin, cause and damage were still under investigation.
deck: The fire began after 11 a.m. at the LTO-NCR facility on G. Araneta Avenue and reached first alarm. Fire investigators had not yet established its origin, cause or damage estimate in the reports reviewed.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: A fire broke out Sunday morning at the Land Transportation Office-National Capital Region building along G. Araneta Avenue in Barangay Santo Domingo, Quezon City.
GMA News, citing a Super Radyo dzBB field report, said the fire began shortly after 11 a.m. and was raised to first alarm.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Firefighters from the Bureau of Fire Protection responded to the incident. As of the initial reporting reviewed by FMB News, investigators were still determining the specific floor where the fire started.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
paragraphs: The cause of the fire and the estimated damage had not been established in the verified reporting reviewed for this article. FMB News is not attributing a cause or stating that specific records, equipment or offices were destroyed without confirmation.
The LTO-NCR had also not announced in the sources reviewed whether services at the affected facility would be suspended, transferred or resumed on a modified schedule.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The LTO-NCR office handles public-facing transport and licensing functions for Metro Manila. Any damage or temporary closure could affect government transactions, but the operational impact remains unconfirmed.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the Bureau of Fire Protection’s investigation findings, an official damage assessment and any service-continuity advisory from the LTO-NCR.

verificationNotes: GMA News reported the fire from a Super Radyo dzBB field report and identified Bureau of Fire Protection responders, the G. Araneta Avenue location and first-alarm status.
Metro Sun Daily independently corroborated the basic incident details and that the cause and origin remained under investigation.
No cause, damage estimate or service-disruption claim is presented as established fact.
